Central discrepancy · Paper proof with recorded review

A complete chronological signed rank ray

Both signed streams are infinite by mortal owner infinitude and the canonical rail. Ordering each stream by date gives a ray containing every residual token exactly once, with one intrinsic endpoint.

Historical paper proofs · Paper proof with recorded review

A complete criterion for the specified charged bounded-shell certificate class

For a fixed eventual rail mask and cap table, the exact residual Hall union yields a sufficient local inequality n−A_v>D_J(v,n;A). Initial cut intervals lose no generality in this specified charged class, and least successful terminal cuts require no extra equality charge.

Central discrepancy · Paper proof with recorded review

A degree-two source multigraph preserves mortal service provenance

The union of two actual matchings can be contracted across virtual same-row pairs. Parallel walks are retained, degree counts multiplicity, and unmatched endpoints stay explicit.

Historical paper proofs · Paper proof with recorded review

A finite multi-cut certificate theorem, with penultimate lag 211 application

The complete reply classification and finite phase-aware induction certificate were independently reconstructed. Distinct bottom cuts require distinct residual top lags. Periodic rails and a replayed finite base prove f(b,b−1)>b+211 for every b≥600.

Source chronology · Paper proof with recorded review

A fourth private source for an old return after three fresh hosts

If q≤T bounds all earlier diagonals, three current fresh hosts precede an old return x≤T, then an increasing private-source path supplies a fourth distinct source for that same x and x+4≤T.

Pell and ordering · Conditional result

A masked positive extremizer has a one-way response with sharp buffer

The response theorem retains explicit masking, direction and buffer assumptions. It is an audited conditional mechanism, not an unconditional game supplier.

Pell and ordering · Conditional result

A record-drop envelope bounds the ordering error

Distinct earlier and later diagonal values fit into intervals bounded by a supplied nondecreasing record-drop envelope. This proves the displayed finite error bounds; a sublinear envelope would give sublinear ordering error. The canonical envelope supplier remains open.

Central discrepancy · Paper proof with recorded review

A reverse-source forest injects C events into forward or missing hosts

Literal MEX supplies a same-row left blocker source. Following reverse hosts strictly decreases physical host and service date, so distinct C paths cannot merge. Forward endpoints may still be unpaid D services.

Source chronology · Paper proof with recorded review

A reversed minimum common source requires smaller private extras

Let x0 be the minimum label in the rightmost fresh host's postbirth history. If an earlier fresh host has not received x0 before its rightmost-host source row a*, it receives a distinct smaller private extra y with a*<y<x0 at that row. Several late hosts require distinct extras.

Density and limits · Paper proof with recorded review

A strict unconditional improvement below the earlier liminf endpoint

A retained rearrangement slack and a local MEX gap cannot both stay small on every logarithmic scale. Their integrated budgets yield a strict liminf improvement, with a deliberately tiny explicit margin.

MEX interfaces · Paper proof with recorded review

A supplied periodic forcing word gives a finite seed-survival decision horizon

A rescued monotone lower process stabilizes to the least periodic immortal queue. Every surviving actual seed contains that core by an explicit finite horizon, independently of appointments farther in the future.

Central discrepancy · Paper proof with recorded review

A surviving mortal diagonal echo has a distinct death-blocker partner

Each currently served old diagonal whose mortal owner is still alive pairs injectively to an actual current service of its death blocker. The remaining signed ledger keeps immortal and dead owners.

Obstructions and counterexamples · Paper proof with recorded review

Abstract counterexample: signed balance does not force pointwise sublinearity

An explicit injective abstract sequence alternates slopes 8/5 and 9/5. It satisfies the reach bound, O(N) signed prefix balance, and eventual scalar cardinality barriers, while Q(n)/n does not vanish. This counterexample does not realize a canonical MEX history.

Central discrepancy · Paper proof with recorded review

An exact death-swap identity, including immediate deaths

For a mortal owner a with death p, K=A(p)+A(a+1)-a equals |S|-|M|+1[p=a+1]. The identity is proved; the proposed inequality K>=0 in C contexts remains open.

Central discrepancy · Paper proof with recorded review

An immortal host has arbitrarily late private blocker services

Infinitely many blockers have victims to the right of any fixed immortal host. Reach bounds push their same-host services arbitrarily far forward. This gives distinct future service sources, but neither free B0 status nor a cut-load bound.

Central discrepancy · Paper proof with recorded review

At a row-sharp birth, the penultimate blocker has an exact rank bound

Distinct survivor outputs fill the exact available interval. Terminal-service capacity then bounds the rank deficit; the conclusion that y=r additionally needs r to be a blocker and no earlier higher diagonal.

Central discrepancy · Paper proof with recorded review

Completed and dated mortal-owner transport retain every endpoint

Partitioning actual blocker hosts gives an exact lifetime defect. Using real service intervals and actual death endpoints gives the dated identity, including backward intervals.

Central discrepancy · Paper proof with recorded review

Completed lifetimes give a weak quadratic negative-energy bound

Actual prebirth services inject into inversions, completed services use a doubled horizon, and deaths have a stated capacity. With P98 this improves a quadratic coefficient without proving subquadratic mass.

Source chronology · Paper proof with recorded review

Component-local signed overlap identity

For two injective rows on the same retained domain, each path changes overlap by the exit-ownership indicator minus the root-ownership indicator, and each cycle contributes zero. When the diagonal drops and the stated MEX coverage holds, every exit is owned and the global identity follows. UnitDip is not an assumption.

Obstructions and counterexamples · Paper proof with recorded review

Counterexample: unit transport delay does not imply pointwise sublinearity

A proved abstract counterexample has delay-one matching, linear crossing stock and linearly large alternating row imbalance. It refutes the general inference to pointwise sublinearity; it is not a canonical Chomp counterexample.

Source chronology · Conditional result

Cross-clock injection into original departure events

Distinct original roots with certified same-transition absent-root relays inject into their endpoint old payload and original endpoint column, across all clocks in one fixed history. Every arising endpoint payload y satisfies y>=3; its charged-root count is at most the number of relay-eligible departure columns, hence at most y-2. For an arbitrary nonnegative payload y, the bound is max(0,y-2), with no arising endpoints when y<3.

Analytic consumers · Conditional result

Dated matching and one-sided variation imply a square-root discrepancy bound

Linear unmatched-token and cut budgets produce square-root block-sum bounds. A bounded upward increment of Q then turns those signed block bounds into pointwise control. All canonical quantitative suppliers remain open.

Pell and ordering · Conditional result

Divergent cumulative relative Pell slack gives sublinear scale defects

The cumulative transfer theorem needs infinitely accumulated relative slack, rather than a strict uniform contraction at every scale. Its game-native slack supplier remains open.

Dated matching and cancellation · Paper proof with recorded review

Dyadic completion has bounded singleton endpoint cost in both window directions

Only unmatched tokens and singleton buckets contribute endpoint defects. A square-root window meets a bounded number of possible singleton scales.

Central discrepancy · Paper proof with recorded review

Every nonrecord high suffix row needs a distinct later actual death

Under tightness, each prebirth service of the future death blocker has a host outside the required survivor-booker roster. Its actual death therefore occurs after the source row and by the birth row.

Central discrepancy · Paper proof with recorded review

Every postdeath diagonal service has an earlier same-host blocker source

For a mortal owner, each service of its diagonal after its death has a unique earlier service of its death blocker in the same column. That blocker source may already be occupied.

Source chronology · Paper proof with recorded review

Exact block ghost laws retain the full older-diagonal history

The exact frozen-label census and full-history overlap ledger give the block-ghost exchange formula and the pool/ghost formula for Q. The revision-2 definitions are essential; these identities do not supply sublinear discrepancy or a density limit.

Analytic consumers · Paper proof with recorded review

Exact C50 lineage identities and the young-root absence relations

Orbit counting and the proved Hosted-to-Pending inclusion give exact old-root and young-root absence identities. Their sum rewrites the C50 defect. Sublinear bounds on the separate fluxes remain unproved, so the asymptotic C50 target does not follow.

MEX interfaces · Paper proof with recorded review

Exact commutation criterion for two MEX insertion factors

When the two first services disagree, both orders select the same pair. A common first service exposes a second-service disagreement exactly when the journals differ above their first common missing label.

Pell and ordering · Paper proof with recorded review

Exact multilevel Pell rigidity on every finite frontier

Oriented gaps obey an exact identity on every finite frontier, with explicit Pell weights for complete decompositions. Under the stated integer-defect and summable-relative-slack conditions, arbitrarily long finite near-rigid rays follow. An infinite canonical ray is not inferred.

Source chronology · Paper proof with recorded review

Exact one-row absence flux for any root class

Partitioning pending owners across consecutive rows proves the exact entrant, exit and switching identity for any fixed root class. Hosted⊆Pending follows from the canonical frozen-blocker partition. No sublinear flux estimate is supplied.

Central discrepancy · Paper proof with recorded review

Exact signed ledger of the current ghost paths

Ghost-owner edges form directed paths. Summing their contributions separates long paths, dead endpoints, inversions and isolated live hosts; none of those terms is silently dropped.

Source chronology · Paper proof with recorded review

Full-history nonpast roots biject with pending diagonal holes

The source map is injective, has image exactly G, and sends each h to a strictly larger label. The resulting finite directed paths give the exact root/exit count. Order preservation between different inputs is not claimed.

Central discrepancy · Paper proof with recorded review

Gap-three birth exposure reduces to three nonnegative slack pairs

Row-sharp and death capacity give an exact slack identity. In a gap-three missing-booker configuration, failure of exposure has only three cases; excluding those cases is still open.

Central discrepancy · Paper proof with recorded review

Higher cells before the penultimate column inject into earlier service rows

A higher current output forces the penultimate value into that column’s earlier private journal. Distinct columns then use distinct earlier rows whose diagonal is above that value.

Density and limits · Conditional result

If a diagonal slope exists, it is below 1.868565865679

A complete reconstructed union-exclusion and MEX service argument bounds any existing diagonal slope. The repaired proof supplies the formerly pending union inequality and the full upper-range exclusion; it does not prove convergence.

Central discrepancy · Paper proof with recorded review

Many earlier diagonal barriers share one current ghost capacity

If a previous diagonal is absent, larger current blockers require earlier bookings or later physical hosts. Every owner violating that capacity must have its own diagonal present now; distinct owners consume distinct current ghost cells.

Obstructions and counterexamples · Paper proof with recorded review

Mortal-only matching cannot pay the required short-block endpoint budget

Every ordered immortal host/owner pair supplies a distinct J or immortal-H2 token. Their quadratic annular mass contradicts a uniform O(N) unmatched budget in all square-root blocks for any mortal-only completion.

Central discrepancy · Paper proof with recorded review

Near-top fresh labels admit only disjoint adjacent swaps

In the record-tight transition each fresh label has one old journal source. A higher award before its new source must use that unique host; two such demands cannot share it. Historical labels are outside the conclusion.

Source chronology · Paper proof with recorded review

No return to a column after a value departs

Once a value leaves a column, it never returns there. A recovery at another column is a MEX event at a host whose earlier journal omits that value; the host need not be newly born. A value present at or below its row index persists forever.

Dated matching and cancellation · Paper proof with recorded review

One fixed dated owner matching gives an exact interval ledger

Actual F/H1 and mortal H2/R source pairs are retained. Earliest D and latest remaining R services maximize each owner’s pairing and minimize its crossing stock at every cut. Immortal and mortal unmatched tokens remain.

Central discrepancy · Paper proof with recorded review

Optimal blocker matching on one ghost path

Every permitted endpoint rearrangement on a path is included. At most one additional pair per path is gained over the owner-only pairing.

Dated matching and cancellation · Paper proof with recorded review

Ordered dyadic cycle completion controls crossings

Sort matched pairs in each dyadic bucket by positive endpoint date before cyclic completion. This adds only a bounded number of cyclic transitions per active scale.

Pell and ordering · Paper proof with recorded review

Pell slack splits exactly into magnitude shortfall and signed cancellation

Decomposing a maximizing Pell window into its three children gives an exact nonnegative slack budget. The identity does not itself supply a positive amount of slack.

Central discrepancy · Paper proof with recorded review

Positive MEX imposes a literal journal ceiling and diagonal capacity bound

Counting the diagonal labels blocked by the journal and current prefix gives a ceiling on every private award. Earlier mortal victims exclude distinct blockers from the journal, yielding a complementary lower service bound.

Source chronology · Paper proof with recorded review

Private ancestry packing across any number of fresh hosts

An old-value return x to the right of j fresh hosts has j distinct earlier private source rows, whose distinct diagonals lie in (x,T]. Therefore j≤T−x. Fresh hosts occur in increasing value order but need not be a physical suffix.

Historical paper proofs · Paper proof with recorded review

Quantitative incompatibility of two counting extremizers

An independently reconstructed paper strengthening of the counting service-budget argument bounds liminf A(n)/n by a degree-eight polynomial root b_new in [0.469,0.471], implying liminf d(n)/n<1.886593095. This is a liminf bound.

MEX interfaces · Paper proof with recorded review

Response content plus one label and one bit reconstructs the ordered journals

The first A-only label identifies the remaining A-membership row, and the membership of mex(A) in B supplies the one missing bit. The phase cannot be discarded for future updates.

Source chronology · Paper proof with recorded review

Saturated private-history handover and a jump of at least 2k

At the rightmost old fresh host in a record row with k fresh labels, its entire strict postbirth private history is permuted into the current right tail. Every matched historical value is at most T−k; if the host has a previous postbirth row, its current column jump is at least 2k.

Analytic consumers · Conditional result

Signed cumulative balance plus downward blocker-clock regularity implies Q=o(n)

Clock regularity spreads a clock spike over a proportional window, contradicting signed balance. Complementarity then rules out plateaus in every scaling limit by a 3/2 owner-capacity expansion, converting clock tracking to pointwise Q control. Both canonical suppliers remain open.

Density and limits · Paper proof with recorded review

Sublinear composed blocker-count defect is equivalent to silver blocker density

The corrected paper theorem equates the composed-count defect with the blocker-density limit under its named counting and lower-density inputs. This is not identified with the stronger ordered diagonal residual without an additional bridge.

Central discrepancy · Paper proof with recorded review

The rank-ray crossing count identifies its exact quantitative gap

At a chronological cut, both edge families have explicit crossing counts. Their width is controlled by the signed prefix imbalance; the construction does not establish the required linear bound.

Central discrepancy · Paper proof with recorded review

The reverse forest cannot terminate at the final blocker source

Every C source precedes the last predeath blocker row; further reverse steps move strictly backward. The rail host zero, whose blocker booking is at p−1, is excluded.

Central discrepancy · Paper proof with recorded review

Tight births have an exact diagonal/blocker predecessor dichotomy

A diagonal birth has a row-sharp predecessor. A blocker birth forces a prior high diagonal and the actual last-row r-to-h death transition. No predecessor F=0 premise is supplied.

Central discrepancy · Paper proof with recorded review

Tight gap-three missing-booker widths at most 18 are excluded at all indices

An authenticated affine rail at column31 forces any tight width≤18 into h≤43. The registered exact initial base excludes that remaining finite slice; widths≥19 remain open.

Historical paper proofs · Paper proof with recorded review

Two bottom cuts exclude penultimate lags through 124

For every b≥500, f(b,b−1)>b+124, giving equality of the neighboring W sets for 0≤k≤124. The argument eliminates lags 121 and 122 by a finite context graph plus all-index descent; fixed-column families pay 123 and 124.

Central discrepancy · Paper proof with recorded review

Two exact inversion-source links

The first inversion copy bijects with actual future-diagonal services. For a mortal inversion owner, the second copy injects into an actual prebirth death-blocker service.

Analytic consumers · Conditional result

Two sublinear suppliers suffice for central discrepancy

The record envelope controls η; uniform Pell-scale discrepancy gives J=o(n). The exact I3 identity then controls central discrepancy at n and d(n).

MEX interfaces · Paper proof with recorded review

Two-owner MEX response has an exact carrier normal form

The sorted two-output pair is the lexicographically first response edge outside the incoming context. Equal edge relations are exactly equivalent to equal carrier responses for every finite context.
